replacements.old: World-agent tabs keep independent session identities and browser-cached transcripts. Macrofold continuations send the existing session identity without resending session configuration (model, harness, billing, provider connection, model parameters, permissions or grants); per-run spending/time limits remain enforced. Existing sessions retain their original configuration, and new conversations adopt current settings. Model availability is checked when creating a session. Hiding retains pending work; closing ends the lane. Transcript restoration creates a fresh conversation identity because backend closure is irreversible. Known recipes and invention jobs have structured cards; question-like prose gets an answer affordance. The existing world agent still has no conjuring or world-mutation tools, and this UI migration does not implement the proposed typed workshop/confirmation backen
replacements.new: The owner World Agent reads durable session/turn records rather than treating a browser-cached transcript as authority. Each paid owner turn/stage uses a fresh native session with scoped application continuity, exact selected tools and the original funding-session identity. Browser storage retains only scoped selections, unsent drafts and unconfirmed request IDs. Hiding or disconnecting does not buy another Run; explicit End revokes future session authority while retaining its history and costs. Supported draft kinds use native validation, exact human review and separate Apply; the Work view adds revision comparison and free structured recipe edits. This is neither unrestricted world mutation nor general conjuring. [Unified owner conversation](world-agent-runtime.md#unified-owner-conversation-interface), [context](world-agent-runtime.md#scoped-context-and-native-save-for-review) and [structured questions](world-agent-runtime.md#structured-human-questions) own the detailed behavior; the older tool-less browser-session narrative is supersede

- [ ] **Separate new-actor initialization from retained prose conversion.** `WorldService` startup calls `migrateCognition`, which calls `migrateKnowledge` in `packages/domain/src/knowledge-migration.ts`. When policy or per-actor knowledge is absent, that path injects `BASE_KNOWLEDGE_POLICY`, moves non-protected inner-world files into a general note and rewrites the originating mind. The same initializer also serves fresh-world/capability creation. Keep legitimate current actor initialization with its authored world owner, but remove older-layout prose conversion and missing-policy substitution from loading; reject incompatible input while retaining its bytes and accounting. Preserve protected identity, normal empty knowledge creation, note revisions and source/privacy semantics. Trace creation and capability callers before replacing this shared initializer; a historical name alone is not proof that all its work is obsolete.
